services.rationale: Prefetch heuristics that help mechanical disks; on an NVMe SSD it pollutes disk I/O and CPU during gameplay. Safe to stop temporarily; Windows starts it again on boot.
Background filesystem indexer. Causes DPC bursts and disk I/O during file scans. Indexer pauses are well-understood; no game depends on it.
Microsoft telemetry. Spikes CPU during ETW flush windows. Stopping it during gameplay is the canonical 'tweak'.

services.display_name: Device Management Wireless Application Protocol Push Message Routing
services.rationale: Device-management push. Irrelevant outside enterprise MDM scenarios.
Submits crash reports. Idle by default but can flush during heavy CPU; harmless to pause.
Print queue manager. Stop only if you don't print during the session. Some games oddly depend on this for the PDF/XPS printer drivers — leave it running unless you've verified.
Compatibility shim service. Triggers occasional disk scans on first-launches; safe to pause.
Retail-display demo; usually disabled already. Pure noise.
Backs the offline Windows Maps app. If you don't use that app, the service does no useful work.

services.display_name: Touch Keyboard and Handwriting Panel Service
services.rationale: Pen/touch input. Irrelevant on most desktop builds. Note: stopping on a 2-in-1 will break the touchscreen — only stop if you don't use it.
Fingerprint / face login support. Pause only if you don't use biometric login during the session.

Background downloader used by Windows Update, Defender definitions, and many app updaters. Pausing during gameplay stops opportunistic downloads from sharing your disk and uplink. Resume restores normal update flow.
Peer-to-peer Windows Update distribution. Uploads update bytes to other PCs on your LAN/WAN — visible network and disk activity during gaming. Safe to pause for a session.
Backs UWP toast notifications. Stopping during gameplay silences Action Center toasts that can pop over a fullscreen game and cause focus loss. Resume restores notifications.
Backs Phone Link, Continue-on-PC, and Nearby Sharing. Periodic Bluetooth/Wi-Fi Direct scans. Pause if you don't use those features during the session.

services.display_name: Windows Media Player Network Sharing Service
services.rationale: DLNA media server for Windows Media Player. Almost no one uses it; idle but listed for completeness.
IoT device discovery (AllJoyn). Effectively dead protocol on Windows 11; safe to stop.
Detects and resolves system diagnostics. Spawns diaghost.exe periodically. Pause for cleaner gaming session; resume restores troubleshooter functionality.
Runs diagnostic libraries on behalf of DPS. Pairs with DPS; pause both together for the full quiet effect.
System-level diagnostic library host. Pairs with DPS / WdiServiceHost.
Repairs damaged Windows Update components and runs reliability checks. Can wake disk I/O at random. Pausing during a session is safe; Windows restarts the service later.
Orchestrates Windows Update install jobs. Pairs with PauseWindowsUpdate — pausing the service plus pausing scans stops update activity end-to-end for the session.
Scheduled disk defrag / SSD TRIM coordinator. Sometimes wakes mid-session; safe to pause.
ICS / mobile-hotspot. If you're not hosting a hotspot, pure background.
Fax send/receive. Vestigial on modern desktops. Safe to stop unconditionally.
Allows remote registry access. Disabled on most installs by default; listed so power users can ensure it's off during gameplay.
GPS / wifi-positioning. Pause if you don't run apps that need location (most games don't).
Xbox Game Bar's recording backbone. Pause only if you don't use Game DVR's instant-clip recording during the session — disabling kills hotkey replay capture.
Smart card reader support (enterprise CACs, etc.). Safe to stop on home builds.
Telephony state management for legacy phone APIs. Effectively unused on desktop.
Printer-driver notification overlay. Pair with Spooler if you've already paused that; otherwise leave running.
Maintains links between NTFS files across volumes. Vestigial on modern Windows; near-zero hits on consumer machines. Safe to stop.
Service for scanners and cameras. Almost no one uses these on a gaming rig. Safe to stop.
Caches SSH keys for the user. Most users don't run ssh during games; the few who do can leave this on.
Background updater + servicing process for Office 365. Periodic CPU spikes when checking for updates. Safe to pause for a session; resume lets Office update on its own schedule.
Triggers scheduled backups (legacy File History / Windows Backup). Wakes disk I/O. Safe to pause; resume re-enables scheduled runs.
Propagates smart-card certificates. No-op on machines without smart-card readers. Safe to stop.
Enumerates smart-card readers for SCardSvr. Pair with SCardSvr / CertPropSvc.
Brokers camera frames between apps. Idle unless you're using a webcam; in that case (streaming) don't stop it.
Auto-connects to wifi/cellular networks. Don't stop on laptops on wifi — wifi will drop. Wired desktops can pause safely.
Wi-Fi connection manager. STOPPING THIS DROPS WI-FI. Listed for wired-desktop users only; default off.

denylist.rationale: Microsoft Defender Antivirus. Stopping AV mid-session is flagged by anti-cheats (Vanguard especially requires AV to be running) and leaves a security gap if framesage crashes. Permanently denied.
Windows Defender Firewall. Stopping the firewall is a real security risk and breaks loopback for many launchers. Permanently denied.
Riot Vanguard. Kernel-mode anti-cheat. Stopping it is the textbook anti-cheat bypass attempt. Permanently denied.
Epic / Tencent Easy Anti-Cheat user-mode component. Same reasoning as Vanguard. Permanently denied.
BattlEye service. Same reasoning. Permanently denied.

FACEIT Anti-Cheat Windows service (ESL FACEIT Group). Stopping it is equivalent to suspending faceitservice.exe — anti-cheat enforcement goes offline mid-session and trips FACEIT's match-watcher. Permanently denied.
DHCP client. Stopping it kills the network. Permanently denied.
DNS resolver cache. Stopping it breaks DNS for online games. Permanently denied.
Network Location Awareness. Required for network state detection; stopping it breaks most networked apps.
Windows Audio service. Stopping it kills game sound. Permanently denied.
Alias for AudioSrv on some Windows versions. Permanently denied.
Hosts Windows Audio device endpoint enumeration; AudioSrv depends on it. Stopping breaks audio device switching and ultimately game audio. Permanently denied.
Remote Procedure Call (RPC). Nearly every Windows service depends on it; stopping it cascades into shell breakage. Permanently denied.
RPC Endpoint Mapper. Required for RPC; same reasoning as RpcSs. Permanently denied.
DCOM Server Process Launcher. Core COM infrastructure that explorer.exe, Wininit, and the SCM itself depend on. Permanently denied.
Group Policy Client. Stopping it can hang login and policy refresh. Permanently denied.
Security Accounts Manager. Required for local account auth. Permanently denied.
User Profile Service. Required for user-profile load/unload. Permanently denied.
Themes / DWM theming. Stopping it disables compositing and visual styles, which can break fullscreen exclusive transitions on some games.
